column2: Peacebloom. The first herb most healers ever learn to pick. It asks nothing of you, and it grows wherever there is a little peace to spare.
Peacebloom again. Some druids keep one pressed in their satchel, just to remember where they started.
Small, white, and everywhere. The world is generous with the gentle things, if you look.
Silverleaf. Turn it in the light and you'll see why it has the name. Small things are worth noticing.
Silverleaf likes the edges of paths. It has watched more travellers pass than any of us.
Hold it up to the moon sometime. It glows almost the same colour.
Earthroot. It likes the feet of hills and the shelter of stones. Steady, patient, and holding on.
Earthroot never hurries. It takes its time, and it takes hold.
Brush the soil from it gently. The hills gave it up for you.
Mageroyal. A proud little flower, for one that grows by the roadside.
Mageroyal. Bright as a little flame, and just as eager.
A royal name for a roadside flower. It doesn't seem to mind which.
Briarthorn. Mind your fingers. Even the thorns are only keeping something safe.
Briarthorn guards itself. Gloves, or patience. Patience is better.
Even the thorny ones are worth the care. Most good things are.
Swiftthistle. It hides among other herbs and comes to you as a small surprise. The alchemists make swiftness from it.
Swiftthistle hides in the shade of other herbs. A small gift for those who look twice.
Quick to find, quick to fade. Enjoy it while it's here.
Bruiseweed. An ugly name for a plant that helps things mend.
A dusty leaf from a dusty slope. The healers will turn it into comfort.
It grows in the hard places, between rocks. Stubborn and kind at once.
Stranglekelp. The sea keeps its own garden. Take a breath before you go down for it.
Kelp, swaying in the current like a slow green dance. Watch it a moment before you take some.
Cold and green and swaying. Even underwater, the world breathes.
Wild Steelbloom. A flower that decided to be as tough as the hills around it.
Steel in the name, petals in the hand. It's allowed to be both.
It grows where the ground is hard. It doesn't complain about it.
Grave Moss. It grows where the dead are laid. Pick it gently. Someone was remembered here.
Grave Moss. Life, even here. Especially here.
Pick it softly. Whoever rests beneath won't mind a little company.
Kingsblood. A grand name for a quiet plant. Kings come and go. The herb is still here.
Kingsblood. Deep red, and proud of it. Every herb has its own way of standing tall.
A royal name for a wild thing. It answers to no king at all.
Liferoot. It follows the water, and drinks from the riverbanks. Where it grows, things are alive.
The sound of running water, and there it is. Liferoot never strays far from a river.
Its name says everything. Life, and roots. What more do any of us need?
Fadeleaf. It prefers the shade, and it's easy to walk past. Most of the best things are.
Fadeleaf. Look away and it's half gone. Look back, and it was always there.
Rogues love it for hiding. You can love it for being quietly lovely.
Goldthorn. It catches the evening light on the hillsides. Take a moment to watch it.
Goldthorn. Gold that grows. The only kind worth having, really.
A thorn with a golden edge. Careful hands, and it gives itself up easily.
Khadgar's Whisker. Named for the archmage, and said to look a little like his beard. Even legends end up as herbs, eventually.
Khadgar's Whisker. Named for a wizard, but it was here first.
Thin and wiry and wise-looking. It suits the name.
Wintersbite. It only grows in the cold of the Alterac Mountains. It bites back, a little.
Wintersbite. It blooms in the cold because nobody told it not to.
Frost on the petals and a bite in the air. Wrap up warm.
Firebloom. It loves the hottest, driest lands, where little else will grow.
Firebloom. It drinks the heat and gives back colour.
Where the ground is scorched, it grows anyway. A little hope in a hard place.
Purple Lotus. A lotus that grows out of hard country. Beautiful things don't always need soft ground.
Purple Lotus. It floats like it has nowhere to be. Take the hint.
Lotus petals open slowly. There's no rushing a flower.
Arthas' Tears. It grows where the plague passed through. Even grief can flower, given long enough.
A pale little flower with a heavy name. It didn't choose the name. It only chose to grow.
They grow where the land was hurt. The land remembers, and it heals anyway.
Sungrass. It spreads across open land under a wide sky. Stand up straight for a moment, and feel the sun.
Sungrass. It holds the light of long afternoons. Take some with you.
Warm to the touch, almost. As if it's been listening to the sun all day.
Blindweed. A plant of the swamps and the deep wet places. The marsh is full of life, if you're slow enough to see it.
Frogs, reeds, the smell of wet earth. Blindweed's home is a busy one.
Careful in the mire. Step where the roots are; they know the ground.
Ghost Mushroom. It glows faintly in the dark places. Even down here, something is growing.
Ghost Mushroom. A little lantern for the dark places.
Quiet down here. The mushrooms keep the caves company.
Gromsblood. Named for Grom Hellscream, who fell, and rose, and paid for it. The land remembers him in red.
Gromsblood. A fierce name. It grows where the land is wounded, and it still grows.
Dark and bitter. Not every gift is gentle, but it is still a gift.
Golden Sansam. Warm in the hand, and worth the walk. The healers prize it.
Golden Sansam. A warm colour for a warm place. Breathe it in.
Some herbs ask to be found. Sansam just waits, glowing.
Dreamfoil. Some say it carries a little of the Emerald Dream in its leaves. A druid would know.
The druids who sleep in the barrow dens walk the Dream for years. A leaf of it is plenty for one afternoon.
Pick it gently, as if you might wake it.
Mountain Silversage. It grows high, where the air is thin and clean. Breathe it in.
Mountain Silversage. Worth the climb. Turn round, if you like, and see how far you've come.
Silver in the leaves and snow in the wind. Worth every step.
Plaguebloom. It grows from tainted ground and turns that taint into medicine. Healing often starts in the worst places.
Plaguebloom. The soil is sick, but the flower still opens. The land is fighting for itself.
Every one you pick is one less sorrow in the soil.
Icecap. A flower of Winterspring's snow. It has learned how to bloom in the cold.
Icecap. It grows under the snow, waiting. Patience made into a plant.
Cold fingers, warm heart. That's how you gather Icecap.
Black Lotus. The rarest flower in Azeroth. Hold it for a moment before you put it away. You may not see another for a long time.
Another Black Lotus. Luck like this deserves a quiet moment of thanks.
Darker than the night sky, and just as full of stars, if you look closely.
Breathe. The forest isn't going anywhere, and neither is the next herb.
Listen for a moment. Wind, birds, water. You're allowed to just be here.
You don't have to hurry. Gathering is a kind of listening.
Look up from the map, if you like. Somewhere nearby, something beautiful is happening that nobody else will see.
Every herb you pick will grow back. That's the oldest lesson in the druid's path.
The world is big, and you are in it. That's enough for today.
Kneel. Pick slowly. Say thank you, if you like. The druids always did.
The roots go deeper than you can see. Somewhere under your feet, the whole forest is holding hands.
Thank you, little one. Nothing of you will be wasted.
Every hunt is a debt. Carry it lightly, and use it well.
Gently now. The beast has given what it had. Its spirit runs on, somewhere green and quiet.
In a few days this will be a cloak, or a quiver. And still, somehow, a little bit wild.
The kaldorei never took more than the forest could spare. Neither do you.
Rest now, friend. The forest will take back what's left.
Your hands know this path now. Let them. The rest of you can simply look around.
Picking, walking, picking. A rhythm like this can hold a busy mind, if you let it.
Peacebloom closes a little at night, like hands folding. Even flowers rest.
A healer's first bandage, a child's first posy. Peacebloom has been both.
Most of a plant is hidden below. For every bloom you see, there's a quiet web of roots holding the soil together.
Bees visit it all day long. You're in good company.
Take a breath before you pick the next one. Peacebloom isn't in a hurry, so neither are we.
That silver sheen is the leaf catching light it can't use, and giving it back to you.
Silverleaf grows best on ground that's been walked. It likes being near travellers.
A small herb with a soft shine. The White Lady would approve.
Every leaf is turned toward the sky, as if listening.
Run a thumb along it. Soft on one side, cool on the other.
Earthroot's roots go down further than its leaves go up. It knows where its strength is.
Smell the soil on it. That's the smell of a living forest floor.
The fine threads on the roots aren't all its own. Some belong to the fungi it trades with, sugar for water.
Hills hold their roots the way old friends hold hands. Quietly, and for a long time.
Steady things are easy to overlook. Not today.
Mageroyal turns its face to follow the sun across the day.
A bright little crown on a thin stem. It carries itself well.
The colour is for the bees. Flowers dress up for their visitors.
It grows by the roadside, where everyone passes and few look. You looked.
Even a small flower can make a clearing feel like a celebration.
Briarthorn's thorns are older than any blade. The world learned guarding from plants like this.
Thorns keep grazing beasts away so the flowers can set seed. Protection, not spite.
Slowly, from the base of the stem. It gives itself up more kindly that way.
Birds nest in thickets like these. The thorns keep the little ones safe.
Being careful with something prickly is a kind of respect.
Swiftthistle's down floats off on the lightest breeze. Every seed a small traveller.
A thistle that's quick to grow and quick to go. Some lives are short and bright.
You found it in another herb's shadow. Good eyes.
It never stays in one place long. The wind is its road.
A little speed in a leaf. Saved for the day you need it.
Bruiseweed grows thick on dry slopes, holding the soil down when the rains come.
Plants like this heal the ground first, and people second.
Crush a leaf, if you like, and smell it. Bitter, green, honest.
Not every helper is pretty. Most of them aren't, really.
Bruises fade. So do hard days. This leaf knows.
Kelp isn't quite a plant. It's an older kind of life, from before roots, drinking light through the water.
Underwater forests sway like this all the time. The sea is always breathing.
Fish shelter in kelp the way birds shelter in trees. A whole village down there.
Come up slowly, and take a good breath. The kelp can wait.
It grips the rocks so the tide can't take it. Holding on, and still moving.
Wild Steelbloom grows in stony ground where softer things give up.
A hard stem and a soft petal. Strength doesn't have to mean being hard all the way through.
The hills around it are made of iron and patience. So is the flower.
Wind-bent, sun-baked, and still blooming. A good teacher, that.
Stand in the wind a moment, like it does. The ground holds you as it holds the flower.
Moss has no roots at all. It holds on with tiny threads, and drinks the rain and dew straight through its leaves.
Mosses were among the first green things to leave the water. They've been softening stone ever since.
A green blanket over old stones. The forest tucking someone in.
Moss can dry out for months and wake with the first rain. Patience, written in green.
Quiet places grow the softest things.
Kingsblood's red comes from the same colours that turn autumn leaves. Sunlight, kept.
It stands up straight among the grasses, as if waiting to be noticed. Notice it.
Plenty of things are named for kings. Few of them grow back every spring.
A deep colour for a quiet field. Like a heartbeat in the grass.
Gather it kindly. Real nobility is gentle.
Liferoot drinks so much that the riverbanks stay firm around it. It gives back by holding on.
Listen. Water nearby. Where water goes, life follows.
Its roots are thick and pale, full of everything it's gathered. A living store for hard times.
Rivers carve the land, and plants like this hold it together. Between them, a valley.
Rinse it in the river if you like. It's at home there.
Fadeleaf has shade leaves: wide and thin, catching every bit of light under the canopy.
In the dim, it wastes nothing. A good way to live through a grey season.
Quiet colours, quiet places. Not everything needs to shine.
Some things are only found by those who move slowly.
Let your eyes adjust to the shade. There's more here than you first saw.
Goldthorn's flowers are shaped for bees. The petals make a landing place, and the nectar's tucked deep.
A golden edge on a thorny stem. The best things are often a little guarded.
Late afternoon light, and goldthorn on the hill. That's a picture worth keeping.
Bees can see colours on its petals that we can't. Paths drawn in light, leading to the nectar.
It's rich in the only way that matters to a hillside: it feeds things.
Thin and tangled, like a beard nobody's combed. It's earned that look.
It grows in the damp and the dappled. Not every wise thing lives in a tower.
A plant named after a wizard. The plant doesn't seem bothered either way.
Wiry things bend instead of breaking. Worth remembering.
Untangle it gently. Hurried fingers tear what patient ones keep whole.
Cold-country plants grow low and slow, keeping out of the wind.
Its leaves are tough and small, holding on to every bit of warmth.
Breathe out and watch your breath hang in the air. Wintersbite lives in that kind of cold, every day.
Snow is a blanket, for plants. Under it, they're warmer than you'd think.
Hard winters make for clear skies. Look up later, if you can.
Firebloom keeps its water close and opens only when it's ready. Desert plants don't waste a drop.
Some seeds in hot lands only wake after a fire. Something new, out of the ashes.
The ground's warm even through your boots. Take a sip of water while you're here.
Bright as embers, but it doesn't burn. It only glows.
In a dry land, every flower is a small promise of rain.
A lotus's leaves shed water like pearls. Nothing muddy sticks to them.
Lotus seeds can wait a very long time before they sprout. They'll open when the moment's right.
It rises clean out of the mud. Where you start isn't where you have to stay.
Purple was a rare colour once, saved for the sacred. Here it's just growing in the open.
Still water, open petals. Let your shoulders open too, if they'd like to.
Plants are often the first to come back to hurt ground. They make it soft enough for everything else.
A gentle flower in a land that's known a lot of pain. Healing starts small.
Whatever the name, the petals are soft. Hold them that way.
Each one you see is the land saying "not finished yet".
Breathe. Even here, the air carries a little green.
Grasses have no need of bees. They give their pollen to the wind, and trust it.
Grass grows from the base, not the tip. Cut it, graze it, and it simply keeps going.
A whole meadow moving together in the wind. Watch it, for a breath or two.
Sungrass smells like long afternoons. Hold some up and see.
Open sky, warm grass, nowhere to be. That's a good moment.
Swamp plants breathe through their stems, sending air down to roots in the mud.
The marsh looks still, but it's one of the busiest places in the world. Listen.
Frogs sing, flies drift, the water barely moves. A slow kind of song.
Mud and shadow, and still it grows. Every place is somebody's home.
Wet boots, quiet mind. There are worse trades.
A mushroom is only the flower of the fungus. The rest of it runs through the ground for a long, long way.
Some fungi glow in the dark. Nobody's quite sure why. A small mystery, shining.
Fungi are the forest's quiet healers. They turn what's fallen back into soil.
Down here, the light comes from the living. That's a comforting thought.
Cave air, cool and still. Rest your eyes in the dim for a moment.
A dark red stem from scorched ground. The land doesn't give up easily.
Gromsblood loves the broken places. Something always grows in the gaps.
It's a hard name for a hardy plant. Both have weathered a lot.
Old stories cling to herbs like dew. You don't have to carry them.
Bitter herbs make strong medicine. That's been true a long time.
Golden Sansam glows like a lamp left on in a window. Someone's expecting you.
Warm colours, warm hands, warm heart. That's the herbalist's way.
It grows in the rich soil of the wilds, where many seasons have fallen and been turned back into earth.
Each one's a little sun you can carry.
Healers have relied on herbs like this for longer than anyone can remember. You're part of that line now.
Dreamfoil's leaves fold gently, as if sleeping.
Druids say the Dream is the world as it might be, untouched. Somewhere, this leaf is perfect.
Pale green and soft as a whisper. Lower your voice, if you like.
Some plants seem to belong to two worlds at once. This is one.
Sleep well tonight. Dreamfoil would want that for you.
Mountain plants are small and close to the ground. Up here, the wind decides everything.
The silver is a coat of fine hairs, keeping out the cold sun and the drying wind.
Sage smoke has long been used to clear the air, and the mind. This one smells of both.
High places make things simple. Air, stone, sky, you.
Look out across the land, if you like. You came a long way up.
Some plants draw poison out of the soil and lock it in their leaves. Gardeners of hurt ground.
Every Plaguebloom picked is a little sickness taken out of the soil.
Strange colours for a strange land. It's still trying to be a flower.
Gloves on. Gentle anyway.
Wounded land heals from the edges in. You're working at one of the edges.
Snow lets light through. Under it, plants keep growing, slowly, in a blue half-light.
Icecap is mostly patience, frozen into a flower.
Your breath on the petals. A little warmth in a cold place.
The stars are sharp up here. Look up, when your hands are warm again.
Cold keeps things. Old snow, old stories, small flowers.
Black Lotus. Hold it under the moon. The petals take the light and keep it.
Rare things are a gift, not a debt. Enjoy this one.
Some herbalists search for years and never find one. Today, you did.
It grows only in the hardest places. Beauty that asks a lot of the ground beneath it.
Quiet, now. Something rare is in your hands.
Wilted Peacebloom. It's had a hard season, but it's still a flower. Gently does it.
Drooping, but rooted. With some rain, it'll stand again.
A tired little bloom. Everyone has days like that.
Stunted Silverleaf. Small for its age, and none the worse for it.
Short stems in thin soil. It did what it could with what it had.
Not every plant grows tall. They all reach for the light anyway.
Marefoil. A new leaf for the herbalist's book. Turn it over and learn its shape.
Unfamiliar herbs are a gift. The world still has things to show you.
Smell it, if you like, and remember it. That's how every herb you know became known.
The first time you hold a herb, it's a stranger. By the tenth, it's a friend.
Marefoil. Even after all this time, the forest keeps surprising us.
Demonsage. A sage that grew where something dark once passed. It made medicine of it anyway.
The name's grim. The plant is just a plant, doing its best in hard soil.
Sage has always been a cleanser. Perhaps this one is cleaning up after someone else.
Darkness passes through places. Green things outlast it.
Careful hands, steady breath. It's only a herb.
Death Lotus. It grows on Hyjal, the sacred mountain, where the World Tree Nordrassil stands.
On Hyjal, the ancestors gave everything to save the world. The flowers grow from that ground.
A grave name for a flower. On Hyjal, endings and beginnings grow side by side.
Hold it a moment. Every flower on this mountain is part of a very old story.
Wisps are said to drift on Hyjal at night. Perhaps one is watching over this flower.
Rare and dark and still a lotus. It opens toward the light like any other.
Frilled Lichen. A lichen is two lives in one: a fungus and a tiny green partner, living as a single thing.
Lichens grow so slowly that a patch the size of your hand may be older than you.
Lichen grows on bare rock and slowly turns it into soil. Every forest started with something like this.
A lucky find, tucked among the herbs. Partnerships often go unnoticed.
Its frills are delicate. Wrap it carefully.
Rosecap. A blush of rose among the green. A small, rare kindness from the ground.
Rare things hide among common ones. Keep looking closely.
A little colour you didn't expect. The best gifts are like that.
Rosecap. Hold it to the light and see the colour deepen.
Found, not taken. That's the herbalist's luck.
Stranglevine. Vines climb toward the light using others for support. Not cruelty, just reaching.
It winds and grips and climbs. Persistence, mostly.
Untwine it slowly. Vines remember how they grew.
A rare tangle. The forest keeps a few surprises close to the ground.
Every vine is a path the plant took toward the sun.
Seeds. A whole plant, folded small and waiting. Keep them somewhere dry.
Some seeds wait years for the right moment. There's no rushing them, and no need.
Plant one, and you'll have given something back to the world.
Uncommon seeds. A little more promise in each one.
Seeds don't all sprout at once. Some wait, in case the first year is a hard one. Wise.
Tend them well. Growing something is a quiet kind of hope.
Unusual seeds. Who knows what they'll become? That's half the joy.
A seed is a promise that hasn't been kept yet.
Hold them in your palm a moment. All that life, so small.
Scarce seeds. Rare, and full of possibility. Plant them somewhere they'll be cared for.
The rarest things often start the smallest.
These ones are precious. A garden is only ever a series of small faiths.
A timberling sprout. Little tree-spirits grow by the lake here. This one's young. Be gentle with it.
Timberlings are part of the forest's own life. Even the sprouts are a little bit awake.
Small, green, and alive. Teldrassil's children come in many shapes.
Look at the shape of the next leaf you see. No two are the same.
A herbalist's hands smell green at the end of the day. That's a good smell to fall asleep to.
The forest isn't a collection of trees. It's one long partnership between roots, fungi, and light.
You're one of the forest's gatherers now. Take only what you need, and say thank you.
Every plant you pass is doing something quiet and remarkable, simply by being alive.
When the gathering's done, rest your hands. They've worked well today.
Slow down a little. The best herbs are found by those who look carefully.
The herbalist's walk is a slow one. That's half the pleasure.
Each plant has its own place in the world. You're visiting each one.
Look at the ground as you walk. There's a whole world down there.
Every herb has a story: where it grows, what it needs, what it gives.
Leave a few behind because the next traveller might need them, and so might the bees.
Look up between herbs, sometimes. The sky's worth a glance too.
Gently now. Every hide was once a living thing.
Take only what you need, and thank what gave it.
Rest now, little one. Your part in the forest is done.
The kaldorei hunt with respect. Every creature is part of the balance.
Nothing wasted. That's the old way.
A quiet thanks, before you move on.
Every life feeds another. That's the forest's way.
